newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo govt says not yet considering move on DKB.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo govt says not yet considering move on DKB.

text.p: The Tokyo metropolitan government is not yet considering what measures it may take against Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), an official of the metropolitan government said on Thursday.
An official in the metropolitan government's bond section said: "Until the facts become clear, there is no way we can consider taking action.
"Generally speaking, if a bank is involved in a scandal, it is possible that the bank will be excluded from underwriting bonds and be removed from managing public funds," the official added.
But the official said it is impossible to consider taking any measures at this point, since it is unclear whether DKB was involved in any illegal action.
The Tokyo metropolitan government is planning to issue 540 billion yen worth of public placement bonds in 1997/98.
DKB's current share in the underwriting syndicate for the metropolitan government's bonds is 7.2 percent.
Tokyo prosecutors raided DKB's headquarters and the homes of several of the bank's officials on Tuesday and Wednesday in a widening probe into a scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd.

A spokesman for DKB said on Tuesday the bank would cooperate with the investigation, which Deputy Chief Prosecutor Kunihiro Matsuo said was linked to the probe into the Nomura payoff and racketeer scandal.
A Finance Ministry official said on Wednesday that the ministry has not yet started considering measures it might take against DKB, a major of underwriter of Japanese government bonds.
